# SQLCipher amalgamation: commit vs. regenerate-in-CI

**Status:** Decided (E0.I7 followup, `skein-2lq9`). **Decision: keep the
amalgamation committed to git.**

## Context

`native/sqlite/amalgamation/{sqlite3.c, sqlite3.h, sqlite3ext.h}` is the
output of running SQLCipher 4.17.0's `./configure && make sqlite3.c` recipe
(documented in full in `native/sqlite/README.md` §3). It is 9.3 MB
(`sqlite3.c` alone) and is checked into the repository rather than fetched
and regenerated by `native/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt` at build time (contrast
with OpenSSL, which *is* fetched and built by CMake per ABI, sha256-pinned
via `native/sqlite/openssl.sha256`).

The alternative considered: drop the checked-in files, add `.gitignore`
entries, and have CMake (or a CI step) run the SQLCipher `configure`/`make`
recipe on every build.

## Decision: commit the amalgamation

### Reasoning

1. **Reproducible builds is a first-class project goal.** The same source
   tree must build byte-identical output
   (`.github/workflows/reproducible-build.yml` double-builds and diffs the
   release APK on every tag). A checked-in amalgamation removes an entire
   class of non-determinism — no dependency on the CI image's `tclsh`
   version, `make` version, or SQLCipher's `configure` probing environment
   variables differently across machines. What's in `git show` is
   byte-for-byte what compiles.
2. **9.3 MB is proportionate.** The repo is already 50+ MB after the wave 0/1
   commits; one more static, rarely-changing blob doesn't move the needle on
   clone time or CI checkout time the way, say, a growing set of test
   fixtures would.
3. **The amalgamation only changes on a deliberate SQLCipher version bump** —
   not routine day-to-day development. Every other file in the tree changes
   far more often. A large-but-static file is cheaper for git to store and
   diff against than a small-but-frequently-changing one.
4. **The regeneration procedure is already fully documented and verified.**
   `native/sqlite/README.md` §3 has had a copy-pasteable recipe since the
   `skein-qz5` spike. As part of this issue we re-ran that recipe from a
   clean tarball fetch on macOS/arm64 and confirmed the output is
   byte-identical (see "Verification" below) — anyone can audit the
   checked-in file against upstream at any time, so committing it does not
   sacrifice auditability.
5. **Regenerating on every build is slow and adds a toolchain dependency.**
   The full `configure && make sqlite3.c` recipe takes on the order of tens
   of seconds and requires `tclsh` (SQLCipher's code generator uses Tcl, not
   just a C compiler) plus a working C toolchain in *every* build
   environment, including every contributor's laptop. `./gradlew
   :app:assembleFossDebug` today needs none of that for the SQLite layer —
   only for the OpenSSL half, which already pays that cost.

### Trade-offs acknowledged (the "no" side)

| | Committed (chosen) | CI-regenerated |
|---|---|---|
| Repo size | +9.3 MB, static | Smaller repo |
| Build speed | No extra step | `configure && make` on every build (toolchain + tclsh required everywhere) |
| Reproducibility | Guaranteed byte-identical from source control alone | Depends on CI environment stability (tclsh/make/compiler versions) |
| Update cost | Regenerate + commit (deliberate, reviewed) | Bump a pinned commit hash |
| Tamper detection | Explicit (see below) | Implicit — any drift shows up as a build output diff, harder to attribute |

We accept the larger repo and the manual-regeneration-on-bump cost in
exchange for guaranteed reproducibility and zero added build-time toolchain
requirements. If SQLCipher bumps become frequent, this trade-off should be
revisited.

## What "regenerate" means, concretely

The pinned inputs (also recorded in `native/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt` §0 and
`native/sqlite/sqlcipher.sha256`):

| Pin | Value |
|---|---|
| SQLCipher version | `4.17.0` |
| Git tag | `v4.17.0` |
| Git commit | `f9788efa8ac4dfed75c03e4756b1666a1d0845da` |
| Release tarball URL | `https://github.com/sqlcipher/sqlcipher/archive/refs/tags/v4.17.0.tar.gz` |
| Release tarball SHA-256 | `79c0e164b9c059e7487bf8f29272f601cca5f3312cc267461f81e349962a5058` |
| Amalgamation generated | 2026-09-20 |

"Regenerate the amalgamation" means: fetch that exact tarball, verify its
sha256, run the `configure`/`make sqlite3.c` recipe in
`native/sqlite/README.md` §3, copy the three output files into
`native/sqlite/amalgamation/`, and rewrite
`native/sqlite/amalgamation/SHA256SUMS.txt` with the new hashes. All of this
is automated by `native/sqlite/verify_amalgamation.sh` — see below.

Bumping the pinned SQLCipher version means updating **all** of:
`CMakeLists.txt` §0 pins, `sqlcipher.sha256`, the three amalgamation files,
and `amalgamation/SHA256SUMS.txt`, in the same commit, reviewed as a unit.

## Tamper / drift detection

Two layers, at different speeds:

1. **Fast, every build:** `native/sqlite/CMakeLists.txt` §0 hashes the three
   checked-in amalgamation files at CMake configure time and compares them
   against `native/sqlite/amalgamation/SHA256SUMS.txt`. A mismatch — from a
   bad merge, a partial edit, or actual tampering — fails the CMake
   configure step immediately with a pointer back to this document. This
   runs on every `./gradlew :app:assembleFossDebug` / CI build, not just
   releases, because hashing three files is sub-second.
2. **Slow, release tags only:** `.github/workflows/reproducible-build.yml`
   runs a dedicated `amalgamation-integrity` job on every `v*` tag push. It
   downloads the pinned SQLCipher tarball fresh, verifies the tarball's own
   sha256, runs the full `configure && make sqlite3.c` recipe, and diffs the
   result byte-for-byte against the committed files (via
   `native/sqlite/verify_amalgamation.sh --regenerate`). This is the
   authoritative check that the checked-in amalgamation actually corresponds
   to the pinned upstream source, not merely that it's internally consistent
   with its own hash file. It is intentionally **not** run on every PR — the
   full regenerate cycle needs `tclsh` provisioned and takes long enough
   (dependent on runner, roughly a minute) that it doesn't belong in the
   fast inner dev loop.

Both checks fail loudly with a message pointing back to this document and
`native/sqlite/README.md` §3.

## Verification performed for this decision

As part of implementing this policy, the regeneration recipe was re-run from
a clean tarball fetch (macOS/arm64, `tclsh` + `make` + `cc` from Xcode CLT)
and diffed against the checked-in files:

```
$ diff -q sqlite3.c      native/sqlite/amalgamation/sqlite3.c       # (no output — identical)
$ diff -q sqlite3.h      native/sqlite/amalgamation/sqlite3.h       # (no output — identical)
$ diff -q sqlite3ext.h   native/sqlite/amalgamation/sqlite3ext.h    # (no output — identical)
```

All three regenerated files were byte-for-byte identical to the committed
ones, confirming the documented recipe is both correct and reproducible
across machines (the amalgamation's C generation is architecture/OS
independent — it's Tcl string processing over the SQLCipher source tree, not
compiled code).
